/v/Authoritarian is a subverse with 10 subscribers. This would almost certainly place it within the subverse category of "Private". There will be three types of subverses once the voting feature is implemented; System, Public, and Private. Only System and Public subverses will have votes that give the community members power to vote out mods (outcome votes / referenda). Private subverses will only have polls, which do not have outcomes.

All users and communities must follow Voat's sitewide rules. These include: No child pornography or other illegal content; No spam; No doxxing; and to some extent, no vote manipulation (mainly with bots / alts is how the rule currently stands on that).

@system subverses additionally must have very limited rule sets (this is based on precedent, and how too much ridiciulous rules were revoked by replacing power-mods). So having a rule like "Hierarchy first" and then banning someone just for criticizing that hierarchy would not be acceptable in a @system subverse (or in a public subverse, probably).

However this is by all considerations a small, insignificant, and therefore private subverse by all classification perspectives I can see. In that case, the mods do have free reign in following the rules. If the rules they select (or their general banning behaviour) are overly censorious, their communities will probably have difficulty growing, seeing as Voat is largely pro-freedom and anti-censorship. But that is their problem and their risk to take.

In short, given the community and the mod you are criticizing, I don't think there is anything wrong here.
